heading: Financial Condition
memo_rationale: The authorization is broad in time, purpose, and records. A corporate-purpose clause does not itself establish a permissible purpose for every individual consumer report. The missing Permission to Release may address this, but incorporation cannot be evaluated without its text. A separate signed authorization is the recommended evidentiary control, not the only conceivable FCRA permissible purpose. [A15]
memo_replacement: Merchant authorizes Buyer to obtain business financial information reasonably necessary to underwrite this transaction before funding and to service, reconcile, or investigate a specific suspected diversion during its term. Requests must be proportionate to that purpose. Buyer shall obtain an individual’s consumer report only with a permissible purpose under the Fair Credit Reporting Act and any required state-law authority, documented separately for the individual and intended use. No general investigation authority permits unlimited recurring consumer-report pulls. Buyer shall provide legally required notices, protect the information under Section 4.7, and comply with applicable accuracy, adverse-action, and dispute duties. Exhibit C does not expand these limits.
current_body: Merchant and Guarantor(s) authorize Buyer and its agents to investigate their financial responsibility and history and shall provide to Buyer any bank or financial statements, tax returns, and other financial documentation as Buyer deems necessary prior to or at any time after execution of this Agreement. A photocopy of this authorization will be deemed acceptable for release of financial information. Buyer is authorized to update such information and financial profiles from time to time as it deems appropriate.
my_note: Adopt the narrowing. Second REFUTATION of our register: FCRA permissible purpose may lawfully sit in the missing Permission to Release, so our finding that Lombard has no FCRA authority is not established. Correct the register, then decide at 101.

heading: Transaction History
memo_rationale: “Continuation in this program” suggests ongoing discretionary credit qualification. After funding, use transaction data for defined servicing purposes; deteriorating financial results are not a fresh underwriting condition.
memo_replacement: Subject to Sections 4.3, 4.7, and 4.16, Merchant authorizes the Approved Processor and Bank to provide transaction history reasonably necessary for underwriting before the Purchase Date and for verifying Purchased Receipts, reconciliation, and lawful servicing thereafter. A decline in sales or creditworthiness after funding does not permit Buyer to revoke the purchase, require repayment, or suspend reconciliation.
current_body: Merchant authorizes the Bank and the Approved Processor to provide Buyer with Merchant’s banking and credit-card processing history from time to time to determine qualification or continuation in this program.
my_note: 'Continuation in this program' does read as ongoing credit qualification, which is off-message for a completed purchase. Cheap fix.

heading: Protection of Information
memo_rationale: The closed recipient list conflicts with §§5.16, 7.15, and 7.23, while the damages release weakens accountability. Establish one controlling policy, purpose limits, vendor controls, retention, correction, and breach response. Financial privacy/security coverage is activity- and data-dependent; do not assume all corporate banking data is consumer nonpublic personal information. [A15, A16]
memo_replacement: Buyer shall use Merchant and Guarantor information only for documented underwriting, servicing, reconciliation, fraud prevention, lawful enforcement, and legal compliance purposes. Buyer may disclose the minimum necessary information to service providers and authorized assignees bound by confidentiality, security, and purpose restrictions; to a credit-reporting or card-network recipient only as permitted by Sections 7.15 and 7.23 and law; and to authorities as law permits or requires. Buyer shall not sell account data or disclose it for unrelated marketing without separate lawful consent. Buyer shall maintain appropriate written safeguards, access controls, encryption, vendor oversight, retention and secure-deletion procedures, and legally required incident response and notices. Merchant and each Guarantor may contact the servicing address to request correction of inaccurate information. This Section controls inconsistent information-sharing provisions and does not waive liability or statutory privacy, reporting, or dispute rights.
current_body: Merchant and each person signing this Agreement on behalf of Merchant and/or as Guarantor authorizes Buyer to disclose information concerning Merchant’s and each Guarantor’s credit standing and business conduct only to agents, affiliates, subsidiaries, and credit reporting bureaus as is required in connection with the Receipts. Merchant and Guarantor(s) waive to the maximum extent permitted by law any claim for damages against Buyer or any of its affiliates relating to any (i) investigation undertaken by or on behalf of Buyer as permitted by this Agreement, or (ii) disclosure of information as permitted by this Agreement.
my_note: Adopt. The closed recipient list contradicts §§5.16, 7.15 and 7.23 — three clauses that each authorise wider sharing. One policy, one purpose limit.

heading: Electronic Account Monitoring Authorization (Plaid)
memo_rationale: Read-only access is protective. Automatic default for loss of connectivity and open-ended ongoing creditworthiness review are unnecessary with processor settlement data. Require alternatives, a named service, and termination/data safeguards; distinguish revoking data access from intentional diversion.
memo_replacement: Merchant may authorize read-only access to identified business accounts through Plaid or another service disclosed before connection, solely for the purposes permitted by Sections 4.3 and 4.4. Buyer shall explain the data categories, service provider, access duration, and revocation method. This authority never permits a debit, transfer, or withdrawal. Merchant may supply equivalent processor reports or account statements if connectivity fails or access is revoked. Buyer shall provide a reasonable alternative and assistance; a lapse, token expiry, bank restriction, or good-faith revocation is not itself an Event of Default. Buyer shall end active access upon completion or termination, retain only records reasonably needed for legal compliance or a specific dispute, and apply Section 4.7 to all obtained data. No bank credentials or raw transaction data may be supplied to industry associations under Section 7.15.
current_body:
Merchant authorizes Buyer to obtain read-only electronic access to the Approved Bank Account through Plaid, Inc. (or any equivalent secure bank-data aggregation service designated by Buyer) for the purpose of (a) verifying Merchant's daily and weekly Receipts during the term of this Agreement, (b) supporting the Reconciliation procedures set forth in Section 3, (c) confirming that the Specified Percentage of Receipts is being properly remitted by the Approved Processor, and (d) ongoing creditworthiness review by Buyer.
Merchant shall (i) authorize the Plaid connection during onboarding, (ii) maintain the connection in active status throughout the term of this Agreement, and (iii) promptly re-authorize if the connection lapses for any reason (including bank-side credential changes or token expiry). Buyer's access via Plaid is read-only; this authorization does not, by itself, authorize any debit, transfer, or withdrawal — collection mechanisms are governed exclusively by Section 2.3 (Split Funding via Approved Processor).
Merchant acknowledges that prolonged loss of Plaid connectivity (more than five (5) consecutive Workdays without Buyer's prior written consent) shall constitute an Event of Default under Section 6.1.1, except that a lapse arising from a cause outside Merchant's reasonable control — including a bank-side credential change, token expiry, or an outage at the aggregation service — shall not be an Event of Default if Merchant re-authorizes the connection within ten (10) Workdays after notice from Buyer.
Buyer agrees to (i) handle all data obtained through Plaid in accordance with applicable privacy and data-protection laws, (ii) limit access to essential personnel only, and (iii) not share Merchant's bank-data with third parties except as required for servicing this Agreement (e.g., the Approved Processor or industry-standard performance reporting per Section 7.15).
my_note: Read-only Plaid access is protective and should stay. Automatic default on loss of connectivity is not defensible when we already receive processor settlement data. Distinguish revoking data access from intentional diversion.

heading: Reporting
memo_rationale: Blanket principal information sharing with undefined associations lacks purpose and accuracy controls. An association may function as a consumer reporting agency depending on what it does; not all business-only reporting is FCRA-covered. Do not report failure to generate receipts as a delinquent fixed debt. [A15]
memo_replacement: Buyer may report accurate business performance information only to a specifically identified reporting organization for a lawful, disclosed purpose, subject to Section 4.7 and applicable law. Before furnishing personal consumer-report information, Buyer shall establish lawful authority and comply with applicable accuracy, adverse-action, and dispute obligations. Buyer shall distinguish a genuine payment diversion from ordinary non-generation of Purchased Receipts and identify a reasonably substantiated dispute where required. Merchant and affected individuals may request the recipient’s identity and correction process. No raw account data, credentials, or unrelated personal information may be shared, and this Section authorizes no marketing or unrestricted association disclosure.
current_body: Buyer and its affiliates are or may become members of one or more industry associations that exchange and share information regarding the performance by merchants under merchant cash advance and related documents. Buyer and its affiliates reserve the right, without further notice to Merchant, to provide information to such industry associations relating to Merchant and its principals, as well as Merchant’s performance under this Agreement and related documents. Merchant, for itself and its principals, authorizes Buyer and its affiliates to provide such information without further notice to or consent of Merchant or its principals.
my_note: Blanket principal-level sharing with undefined 'associations' has no purpose limit and no accuracy control. The operative rule: never report failure to generate receipts as a delinquent fixed debt — that single sentence is the FCRA exposure.

heading: Communications, Recording, and Premises Access
memo_rationale: Signing for a company cannot safely supply every call participant’s recording consent. Separate optional marketing from necessary servicing; “required to service” is not a blanket TCPA exception. Do not describe the vacated one-to-one marketing rule as current law. As of this review, the FCC’s cross-topic informational revocation requirement is deferred until January 31, 2027, while core revocation duties remain. Premises access should require consent or lawful process. [A17, A18]
memo_replacement:
Buyer may contact Merchant and a separately identified Guarantor for administration and lawful servicing using methods permitted by applicable law. Any consent required for automated calls, artificial or prerecorded voice calls, or texts shall be obtained from the person legally entitled to provide it for the specified number. A recipient may revoke consent by any reasonable means, including STOP, telephone, or email. Buyer shall honor revocation within the legally required period; servicing or collection does not by itself preserve consent. Any further contact must use a lawful method or applicable exemption.
Marketing consent, if requested, shall be obtained separately, identify the authorized caller and number, contain required disclosures, and be optional and not a condition of funding. This Agreement supplies no blanket do-not-call override or consent for unspecified affiliates. Before recording a call, Buyer shall give required notice and obtain legally sufficient consent from each participant, with an unrecorded alternative when practicable. Buyer may visit Merchant’s premises only on reasonable advance notice and with contemporaneous consent, or under lawful court authority, without force, disruption, or breach of the peace.
current_body:
Buyer may monitor and/or record any telephone call between Buyer and any Merchant or Guarantor, or any of their respective owners, employees, or agents. By signing this Agreement, each Merchant and Guarantor agrees that any such call may be monitored and/or recorded.
Each Merchant and Guarantor expressly consents and authorizes Buyer, its servicers, and their respective subsidiaries and affiliates to call, send text messages, and/or send other electronic messages (including prerecorded or artificial voice messages) using an automatic telephone dialing system to any telephone number provided by any Merchant or Guarantor in this Agreement or any application for funding, including cellular phone numbers and landlines, regardless of their inclusion on any do-not-call list, for purposes of servicing, collections, marketing, or promoting any product offered by Buyer.
Each Merchant and Guarantor are not required to consent to the marketing portion of the foregoing as a condition of qualifying for or obtaining the funding under this Agreement. To opt out of marketing or promotional contact, Merchant or Guarantor may notify Buyer in writing at the address set forth in Section 7.3.
Each Merchant and Guarantor may revoke the consent given in this Section at any time by any reasonable means, including by replying STOP to a text message, by telephone, or by email to the address in Section 7.3, and Buyer will honour the revocation for all contact that is not required to service this Agreement. Revoking consent does not affect any other right or obligation under this Agreement.
Each Merchant grants Buyer the right to enter and observe Merchant's premises during business hours, without prior notice, at any time after the occurrence of an Event of Default, for the purpose of protecting Buyer's interest in the Receivables and the Collateral.
my_note: Adopt. A corporate signature cannot supply every future call participant's recording consent, and 'required to service' is not a TCPA exception. The memo is careful and current on the FCC position — the cross-topic revocation deferral to 31 Jan 2027 is a deferral, not an exemption. Do not restate the vacated one-to-one rule as live law anywhere in our materials.

heading: Independent Sales Organizations and Brokers
memo_rationale: An “independent” label cannot determine actual/apparent agency or erase statutory responsibility. The merchant indemnity for the ISO’s acts is reversed risk allocation, and a promise merely to request an ISO refund may fail if the ISO disappears. The replacement gives a direct Buyer remedy for an unauthorized Buyer-engaged channel fee; that refund promise is a recommended commercial safeguard. Verify any anti-lead-list marketing separately. [A12, A14, A23]
memo_replacement:
Section 1 shall identify any ISO or broker involved in this transaction, its role, compensation, payor, and any disclosure required by law. An ISO may be an independent contractor, but that description does not waive responsibility arising from actual or apparent authority, Buyer’s conduct, or applicable law. Buyer shall maintain reasonable onboarding, licensing or registration verification, training, monitoring, complaint, and compensation controls for its channels. Merchant and Guarantor do not indemnify Buyer for an ISO’s acts or omissions.
An ISO engaged by Buyer may not charge or collect compensation from Merchant beyond the amounts expressly permitted, disclosed, and agreed under applicable law and Buyer’s stated no-direct-ISO-fee policy. Buyer shall investigate reported unauthorized charges promptly and refund a substantiated unauthorized charge collected by its engaged ISO within ten Workdays after substantiation, without requiring Merchant to recover from the ISO first. Buyer may separately pursue the ISO. Nothing disclaims legally attributable representations or limits claims for deception or unauthorized fees.
current_body: Each Merchant and Guarantor acknowledges that Merchant may have been introduced to Buyer by, or received assistance in entering into this Agreement from, an independent sales organization, broker, or marketing affiliate (“ISO”). Each Merchant and Guarantor agrees that any ISO is separate from and is not an agent or representative of Buyer, and that Buyer is not bound by any promises, representations, or agreements made by any ISO that are not expressly contained in this Agreement. Each Merchant and Guarantor agrees to indemnify and hold harmless Buyer and its officers, directors, members, shareholders, employees, and agents from and against all losses, damages, claims, liabilities, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees and expert fees) resulting from any act or omission by any ISO. Buyer’s agreements with its ISOs prohibit an ISO from charging, accepting or soliciting any fee or other consideration from a merchant in connection with any financing; the commission Buyer pays is the ISO’s entire compensation. Merchant is therefore not required to pay any ISO anything as a condition of this Agreement, and should notify Buyer at once if any ISO asks it to. If Merchant nevertheless pays an ISO a fee, Buyer will on notice require the ISO to refund it to Merchant.
my_note: An 'independent' label does not determine actual or apparent agency, and merchant indemnity for the ISO's acts is backwards risk allocation. Give the merchant a direct remedy against us for an unauthorised channel fee — we can recover from the ISO; the merchant cannot.

heading: TMF/MATCH Reporting Consent and Release
memo_rationale: The current text already conditions reporting on network rules and law; it does not expressly permit false reporting. Remove the sweeping release, identify the authorized reporting actor, require actual criteria and corrections, and prohibit payment-pressure threats. The FRPA does not establish that an MCA default itself is a network reportable event. Obtain current acquirer/network rules. [A24]
memo_replacement: Only a party authorized under the applicable card-network rules may submit a MATCH, TMF, or similar report. Any report shall be based on documented facts satisfying the applicable reporting criteria, use accurate required information, and comply with law and Section 4.7. Buyer shall not report or threaten to report Merchant or a principal solely to pressure payment of a disputed MCA claim or because receipts declined. Buyer shall identify the reporting entity and available dispute or correction channel when law and network rules permit, and cooperate promptly in correcting inaccurate information. Merchant and Guarantor do not release claims for inaccurate, unauthorized, negligent, malicious, or unlawful reporting.
current_body: Merchant acknowledges and consents that, in connection with this Agreement and any related processor relationship, Buyer or its assignees, servicers, or processor partners may report Merchant or any of its principals to industry-standard databases including but not limited to the Member Alert to Control High-risk Merchants (MATCH) database operated by Mastercard and the Terminated Merchant File (TMF), where such reporting is permitted by applicable card-network rules and applicable law. Merchant waives and releases Buyer and its assignees, servicers, and processor partners from any claim arising from such reporting that is consistent with applicable law and card-network rules.
my_note: Adopt, with emphasis on one point: the FRPA does not establish that an MCA default is a network-reportable event at all. Pull the current acquirer and network rules before anyone reports anything, and prohibit MATCH threats as collection pressure outright.

memo_rationale: The actual release is missing, so one cannot conclude Lombard lacks all FCRA authority or that the existing release is compliant. Require entity/individual identity, precise permissible uses, duration, recipients, and statutory notices; a business signature cannot authorize another person’s report. The replacement addresses the reference only. [A15, A16]
memo_replacement: Any Permission to Release Information shall be provided in full before signature, separately executed by the person with authority over the information, and limited to the purposes and safeguards in Sections 4.3, 4.4, and 4.7. It shall identify Buyer as Lombard Capital LLC, the information sources and categories, permitted uses, duration, and applicable correction and notice rights. Individual consumer-report authority shall be separately established and documented under applicable law; a Merchant signature does not authorize reports on nonsignatory individuals. No release authorizes unrelated marketing, unrestricted disclosure, waiver of statutory rights, or collection powers beyond this Agreement. The complete signed release shall be attached to the transaction record and delivered to the signer.
current_body: A Permission to Release Information shall be executed by Merchant as a separate signed instrument authorizing Buyer to obtain trade, landlord, and bank information from vendors, suppliers, landlord/mortgagor, banks, creditors, brokers, and payment processors for the purposes of underwriting, ongoing program qualification, and post-default collection. The form of the Permission to Release Information is attached and incorporated by reference, and shall be executed contemporaneously with this Agreement.
my_note: Adopt. And note the refutation at 020: because the Release was never supplied, we cannot conclude Lombard lacks FCRA authority — nor that what exists is compliant. Require identity, precise permissible uses, duration, recipients and statutory notices, and note a business signature cannot authorise another person's consumer report.
